rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative first candidate built from the contract's physics and scoring. Speed: the course is about 4 to 5 m and must finish in under 3 s, so average speed needs to be roughly 1.5 m/s or more. I set base_speed to 1.8 (PWM fraction 0.9) to leave some margin for the speed losses that cornering and slip cause. Sensing: five sensors at 0.02 m spacing (x = -0.04 to +0.04) with 0.012 m footprints give a continuous read across the 25 mm tape, even when the robot is 1 to 2 cm off-centre. They sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the steering reacts before the wheels reach the bend. Weights are -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 (positive = left), so the signal grows linearly with lateral error and its sign steers the robot back toward the line. Control: kp = 1.5 gives a turn of about 1.5 x signal, so a full-scale error (signal about 1) produces roughly 525 PWM of differential, which is firm but not saturating. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd = 0.05 adds mild damping. Because signal changes quickly, a larger kd would amplify sensor noise. Line loss uses last_direction so the robot keeps turning the way it was heading when the line disappears. Geometry: wheel_track 0.12 and wheel_radius 0.03 give a moderate turn rate; mass 0.8 kg with body 0.16 x 0.12 m gives moderate yaw inertia; body_width 0.12 keeps the off-track limit at 0.06 m. Expected result: the robot should complete the course with few line losses, but it may show some oscillation on the slalom because kd is low and kp is untested. Hypotheses to test next: (1) kp around 1.5 is enough to hold the line at 1.8 base speed without much oscillation; (2) line losses should be near zero with five sensors; (3) if max_error approaches 0.06 on the tightest bend, speed is too high or kp too low. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness, so the next iteration can separate speed-limited failures from steering-limited ones.
